Referral Note (primary care)

Mrs. Holloway, a 74-year-old retired accountant, is referred for psychiatric evaluation at her daughter's request. Her daughter reports worsening memory over the past three years: she repeats questions, forgets recent conversations, and misplaces household items, and she recently became lost while driving to a familiar grocery store. She now needs increasing help from her daughter with finances and medications. Mrs. Holloway acknowledges some forgetfulness but feels it is a normal part of aging. Medical history is notable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, treated with lisinopril and atorvastatin. No psychiatric history. Referred for evaluation and treatment recommendations.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Appropriately dressed and groomed. Accompanied by her daughter.

Behavior: Pleasant and cooperative. Turns to her daughter for help with several answers.

Speech: Fluent.

Mood / Affect: Mood euthymic.

Thought / Perception: Thought processes logical. Denies hallucinations.

Cognition / Insight: Oriented to person and place; incorrectly identifies the current month. Short-term memory impaired; recent recall poor. Insight into her deficits limited.
